forgemint.heldOutClaim: The held-out answers were not in the spec given to the model (hash-disjoint); anyone can re-run it.

rerun.line: Anyone can now re-run a shared scorecard on a clean GitHub runner with the CI re-run rail: it recomputes every recorded number, checks that the CI run a scorecard names really made that exact scorecard, rebuilds the model with Ollama, runs the held-out set again, and fails the job on any mismatch.

forged.label: a re-hashed, re-signed forgery carrying the genuine run's link

rerun.how: fallforgemint rerun/proof, 2026-09-28: genuine.json minted in CI (run 36431565425), 4/5 vs base 0/5; the forgery recomputes every number but the run it names made a different scorecard; tampered.json and forged.json derived in the open by make-tampered.mjs. GitHub keeps a run's upload about 90 days; after that the rail confirms only that the named run was the rail and was running when the scorecard was stamped, and says so

ownVsRent.claim: At high utilisation, owning inference ran ~6× cheaper per million tokens than cloud GPU instances and ~17× cheaper than a hosted reasoning-model API; breakeven ~5.2 months against on-demand cloud. Below roughly 5 hours a day of use, renting can win.
ownVsRent.short: ~6–17× cheaper to own at high use — renting wins below it
ownVsRent.source: Lenovo Press LP2368, “On-Premise vs Cloud: Generative AI Total Cost of Ownership (2026 Edition)”, 24 July 2026

slm.claim: Small language models are “sufficiently powerful, inherently more suitable, and necessarily more economical for many invocations in agentic systems.”
slm.source: Belcak et al., NVIDIA Research, “Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI”, arXiv:2506.02153, June 2025

modelCollapse.claim: Training on model-generated content causes irreversible defects “where tails of the original content distribution disappear.”
modelCollapse.source: Shumailov et al., “The Curse of Recursion: Training on Generated Data Makes Models Forget”, arXiv:2305.17493 (Nature, 2024)

thesis: As models train on their own output they lose the tails of the distribution. A mesh of real people doing real work is the tails — the clean signal a monolith averages away. Owned, provable models are how that signal is kept, and a receipt that can fail is how anyone trusts it.
